purpose: build reliable pipelines that move and prepare data, so analysis and products can trust it
entry_criteria: Sources, targets and ownership are identified
procedure: Define each dataset's owner, schema, freshness target and quality rules before building.
Build pipelines to be rerunnable and idempotent, so a repeat run gives the same result.
Validate data at entry and at each stage: types, ranges, uniqueness and referential checks, with bad records set aside.
Apply privacy rules in the pipeline: masking, minimization and retention.
Record lineage and run metadata, and alert on failures, late data and volume anomalies.
Test with sample and edge-case data, including late and duplicate records, and document recovery steps.
acceptance_criteria: Bad records are set aside and counted
Privacy rules are applied in the pipeline
Late, failed and anomalous runs raise alerts
validation_method: Data owner and data engineering lead review.

validation.command: python -m pipelines.run --date 2026-01-01 && python -m pipelines.run --date 2026-01-01 && python -m pipelines.check_counts   # example
validation.expect: row counts equal after the second run

validation.check: inject a record with an invalid value and a duplicate
validation.expect: the invalid one lands in the quarantine, the duplicate is dropped

failure_modes.response: Use keys or replace the partition

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A daily orders pipeline replaces its date partition on every run, quarantines rows with negative quantities, masks email addresses before the warehouse load, and alerts when the volume falls 30 percent below the weekly norm.
